properties.decision:
UNDECIDED — RECORDED AS BRAINSTORMING, NOT AS A PROPOSAL. Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16: "this is a hypothetical question, not a go do this (yet)."

DISTINCT FROM THE TWO THE GUARD NAMED, both read. `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` is ACCEPTED and settles WHAT reflow2's decomposition is; this is the OPEN question of whether to run the experiment that decision PLANNED. `dec:idea-should-reflow2s-own-design-be-re-derived-through-a-principled-se-process` asks whether to DECLARE the missing contracts by hand; this asks whether to RECOVER them mechanically and, more importantly, what running adopt would MEASURE about adopt. Three different acts.

⚠️ THE EXPERIMENT WAS ALREADY PLANNED AND NEVER RUN, and how it was recorded is itself the finding. `dec:bl83a-functional-decomposition` names two follow-ons IN ITS RATIONALE — **BL-83b** ("the retired crate view is recovered by adopt-on-a-copy") and **BL-83c** ("the divergence measured by `compare_designs`"). Neither appears anywhere else; there is no second design on disk. A plan reflow2 made for itself in July 2026 is reachable only by reading the reasoning of a decision about something else. THAT IS HOW I MISSED THE FUNCTIONAL DECOMPOSITION TWICE THE SAME DAY. This node exists partly so BL-83b stops being unfindable.

WHAT THE DESIGN ALREADY PREDICTS, verbatim: "A functional carving comes from the product's purpose (a genesis input), not the code, and cuts across crate boundaries, SO ADOPT ON THE CODE CAN ONLY RE-DERIVE THE MODULE VIEW." An adopt pass would reconstruct something close to the `reflow2-core` / `reflow2-mcp` / kit grouping — precisely the view retired in July.

⛔ IN PLACE IT WOULD BE DESTRUCTIVE, which makes "on a copy" non-negotiable rather than tidy. Adopt instructs "build one export document and `import_graph` it once". Importing into a live 2,404-node graph MERGES: `cmp:*` ids collide, recovered module parents overwrite the functional ones, and a property once written cannot be removed. One-way door.

ADOPT'S PREMISE ALSO DOES NOT HOLD: it is for a system "with little or no requirements documentation", and reflow2 has 175 Requirements and 389 Decisions. Its central discipline — "never infer a Requirement from the implementation that satisfies it" — means every requirement it recovered would be satisfied by construction, strictly WORSE than the authored ones present.

⭐ BUT ADOPT IS GOOD AT EXACTLY WHAT REFLOW2 LACKS. Phase 1 insists on "both sides of every contract — this is where the structural findings come from". That is the 73 coupled pairs with ZERO declared interfaces. Recovering contracts from imports and calls is what adopt's scan is FOR.

⭐⭐ THE ARGUMENT THAT MAKES IT WORTH DOING, and it is not self-hosting theatre: IT WOULD BE A GROUND-TRUTH TEST OF ADOPT ITSELF. Every adopt trial so far ran against a system whose true design nobody knew. reflow2 is the ONE system where the answer is known and recorded. `compare_designs` exists; `dec:design-diff-vocabulary` makes the comparison directional and banded. No other trial can ask "how far is the recovered model from a design we know is right?"

A FALSIFIABLE PREDICTION, recorded so the experiment can disconfirm it rather than be narrated afterwards: HIGH structural agreement (modules and couplings are visible in the code), NEAR-ZERO functional agreement (the eight boxes are not in the file tree), and a RECOVERED CONTRACT SET reflow2's own graph does not have. The third is the prize; the second would be a real finding about adopt's limits on functionally-carved systems.

THE OPTIONS: (a) do not run it — the outcome is largely predicted and the cost is real; (b) run on a copy purely to harvest recovered contracts, discarding the rest; (c) run on a copy and MEASURE divergence with `compare_designs` — BL-83b plus BL-83c as planned; (d) run it and publish the comparison as the demonstration.

⚠️ PRECONDITION FOR (b)–(d): the copy must carry a DISTINCT `graph_id`, or the sync machinery treats two designs as one — a trap already recorded from the flo2 work.

NOT ESTABLISHED: whether recovered contracts would be USABLE as-is or would need the same human judgement declaring them by hand needs. If the latter, (b)'s value collapses and only (c)'s measurement survives.
properties.name: OPEN — should adopt be run on reflow2 itself, on a copy, as the one available GROUND-TRUTH test of what adopt recovers?
properties.rationale: Recorded as brainstorming on Anthony's hypothetical, 2026-08-16, at his instruction to capture it. His question; the measurements, the prediction and the destructiveness analysis are mine. Kept at `proposed` rather than promoted, because he framed it explicitly as a hypothetical and not as intent. Its sibling is `dec:idea-genesis-reflow3-from-the-requirements-alone`.
